title: GenAI-Assisted Writing and Academic Performance: Evidence from the Social and Behavioral Sciences
abstract: arXiv:2510.02408v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: This paper studies how Generative AI (GenAI)-assisted writing is associated with peer-reviewed publication output and journal placement in the social and behavioral sciences. We select lexical markers whose frequency rose sharply after ChatGPT's release in late 2022 and classify authors as GenAI-assisted writers when the share of these markers in their papers' titles and abstracts rises relative to their own pre-release baseline. Using matched author-level panel data and a difference-in-differences design, we estimate a 72% increase in publication output among GenAI-assisted writers relative to matched comparison authors in 2025. Across alternative specifications, the estimates range from roughly 52% to 88%. Mean journal placement based on the SCImago Journal Rank (SJR) improves by roughly 1%, but this modest increase is less consistent across different specifications. translated_title: 生成式AI辅助写作与学术表现：来自社会与行为科学的证据
translated_abstract: 本文研究生成式人工智能（GenAI）辅助写作与社会及行为科学领域经同行评审的论文产出及期刊层次之间的关系。我们选取了在2022年底ChatGPT发布后出现频率急剧上升的词汇标记，当这些标记在作者论文标题与摘要中的占比相对于其自身发布前的基线上升时，即将该作者归类为GenAI辅助写作者。基于匹配的作者层面面板数据和双重差分设计，我们估计GenAI辅助写作者在2025年的论文产出相对于匹配的对照作者增长了72%。在不同设定下，估计值范围约为52%至88%。基于SCImago期刊排名（SJR）衡量的平均期刊层次提升约1%，但这一小幅提升在不同设定下的一致性较低。在作者的年度论文组合中，最高层次……（原文在此处截断）
tldr: 研究发现，被识别为使用生成式AI辅助写作的学者，其2025年论文发表量比匹配对照组高出约72%（不同设定下为52%–88%），但期刊质量的提升仅为约1%且不够稳健。
en_tdlr: GenAI-assisted writers in the social and behavioral sciences show roughly a 72% increase in publication output in 2025 relative to matched controls (estimates range from 52% to 88%), while gains in journal quality remain modest at about 1% and less consistent.
